intro: Video editors often ask what do video editors charge per hour, but the answer is rarely a simple number. Instead of focusing on an hourly rate, you should look at your total project impact. This guide explores how to calculate your worth, structure your pricing, and manage your business on your Mac.

blocks.text: The reality of what do video editors charge per hour

When you search for what do video editors charge per hour, you will see a wide range. Beginners might charge $30, while senior editors command $150 or more. This range exists because hourly rates do not account for the specific value you bring to a project. If you only track time, you are selling your capacity, not your expertise. Many editors find that hourly billing penalizes efficiency. If you get faster at editing, you earn less money for the same result. This is why many successful freelancers move to flat-fee pricing based on the value they deliver to the client.
Why hourly pricing leads to burnout

Hourly pricing creates a disconnect between your effort and your income. You spend hours on file management, client emails, and feedback rounds. These tasks are essential, but they are often invisible to the client. If you do not bill for these, you are essentially working for free. Research shows that 62% of full-time creators report severe burnout. A major factor is the pressure to keep hourly rates low to stay competitive. When you compete on price, you are treated as a commodity. Clients will choose the cheapest option, and you will eventually find yourself unable to cover your costs.
The hidden costs of freelance editing

You have many costs that clients never see. Hardware depreciation on your Mac is real. Software subscriptions for Adobe Creative Cloud or plugins add up quickly. Storage costs for large 4K footage files are significant. When you calculate your rate, you must include these overheads. If you ignore them, you are not actually making a profit. Many editors fail to calculate a baseline hourly floor rate. This rate should cover your bills, your taxes, and your savings for retirement. If your current rate does not cover these, you are losing money on every project.
How to fix your pricing strategy

items: Adopt value-based pricing: Charge for the commercial impact of the video, such as increased sales or brand awareness.
Use tiered proposals: Offer three options to every client. This anchors their perception of value and gives them choice.
Package your services: Stop selling just editing. Include research, hook writing, and performance strategy to become a partner.
Implement clear contracts: Define the scope of work explicitly to avoid scope creep and unbilled revision rounds.
Track your time: Use tools to see where your time goes, even if you bill by the project. This helps you estimate future work accurately.

blocks.text: Using your Mac to manage your business

Your Mac is a powerful tool for more than just editing. You can use it to manage your business and increase your efficiency. Applications like Canva are excellent for creating professional pitch decks that highlight your value. Keeping your files organized with Hazel can save you hours of manual work every week. When you spend less time on admin, you have more time for creative work. This is where tools like Lazur can help you get more done in less time.

faq.question: What is the best way to transition from hourly to flat-fee pricing?
faq.answer: Start by tracking your time for a few projects to understand your average effort. Then, estimate the value you provide to the client. Propose a flat fee that reflects that value, ensuring it covers your time, overhead, and profit margin.

faq.question: How do I deal with scope creep in my projects?
faq.answer: Define the scope clearly in your contract. Specify the number of revision rounds included in the price. If the client asks for more, provide a clear quote for the additional work before you start.

faq.question: Should I charge more for rush projects?
faq.answer: Yes. Rush projects require you to shift your schedule and may involve working outside of normal hours. A premium fee for quick turnaround is standard practice.
